title: Man. Post. Cap. X tip — Christ’s cross-merit comes by free imputation, not by the Deuteronomy hanging-law
pass_a_gloss: No statute ordered Christ to the cross. So the obedience he rendered on that cursed tree is not counted to us by that hanging-law, or by law at all, but solely by grace under the Gospel promises.
pass_b_english: For there was no law which ordered that Christ be driven to the cross; nor is the imputation to us of the obedience rendered by Christ on that cursed cross according to that law, or according to law, but from mere grace, according to the promises of the Gospel.
source_text: Nulla enim lex fuit quae iuberet Christum in crucem agi, nec sic nobis imputatio obedientiae a Christo in maledicta illa cruce praestitae est secundum illam legem, aut secundum legem, sed ex mera gratia, secundum promissiones Evangelii.

choices.choice: Cross-obedience imputed by gospel grace, not by that law

notes: Cap. X reatus densify section 700 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 367–368 tip).
